title: Aggrega Core (Provider)
description: Global plugin registrar mapping a rendering engine name to an executable.

version.description: Strict Semantic Versioning of the Provider registrar (e.g., 1.0.0).

description.description: A concise, one-sentence summary of what the entity does.

maintainers.description: List of maintainers who own this entity.

repository.description: The URL to the Git repository where the source files live.

home.description: The URL of this entity's home page, wiki, or documentation.

keywords.description: A list of descriptive keywords for UI discoverability.

deprecated.description: Indicates whether this entity is deprecated and should no longer be used.

plugin.description: Reserved. Names the Wasm rendering plugin intended to render this format (e.g., 'hub.aggrega.ai/providers/helm-renderer:1.0.0'). The compiler does not consume this field today — provider dispatch is by provider name; the Wasm binding belongs to the future plugin entity.

baseSchema.description: JSON Schema 2020-12 defining the keys this provider understands in generative (sourceless) mode. When a Recipe omits the source field, the compiler validates the valuesMapping output against this schema. The IDE/LSP reads it for autocomplete. If absent, the provider does not support generative mode — all Recipes must have a source. See vocabulary/compact-form-authoring.md for the authoring surface.

workloadSchema.description: JSON Schema 2020-12 documenting how this provider translates the aggrega.ai/v1alpha1 Workload kind into provider-native manifests. When present, the provider supports Recipes that declare a workload: block (synthesized mode) — the compiler synthesizes provider-native manifests via a Go Engine, informed by this schema as documentation/contract. When absent, the provider does NOT support Workload synthesis; any Recipe for this provider that declares workload: is rejected at Recipe load time with a clear error. Today the field acts as a presence flag (any non-empty body indicates support); the body becomes executable input to Wasm translators in a future iteration.
